messages:
Jordan: Heads-up — I'm sketching a proposal for per-org rate enforcement that mixes RPM/TPM with a small concurrency cap + burst tokens. Trying to avoid the 'all-or-nothing' behavior we've seen.
Maria: SGTM. can you outline how the hybrid would behave on sudden fan-out from a client (eg, 50 parallel warm streams)?
Jordan: Sure. idea: baseline RPM + TPM limits enforced at the API gateway, plus a soft concurrency cap per org at the runtime router. concurrency cap triggers lightweight queuing (100ms-2s) and only rejects when queue + active > cap + burst_tokens. burst control = token bucket per-org with small burst_tokens (e.g., 5) and refill tied to rpm.
Kevin: Question: where do we measure TPM? tokens or bytes? TPM has bitten us before because embeddings use tokens differently.
Jordan: TPM = tokens/min across generation endpoints. embeddings counted as tokens too (embedding tokenization) to avoid bypass. we also keep a separate embedding-specific quota to be safe.
Asha: How do we avoid head-of-line blocking if we queue on router? streams with long-lived responses could stall others.
Jordan: Good point. router queues only for short-lived requests (<= 5s expected). we mark streaming requests and route them to a separate concurrency pool (smaller cap). also prioritize small inference requests in the queue.
Maria: Implementation plan? gateway enforces RPM/TPM (fastpath rejects), router enforces concurrency + burst tokens, runtime still tracks per-key concurrent KV cache usage for fairness.
Kevin: Telemetry: we need metrics for rejects (rate_limit.type = rpm|tpm|concurrency|burst), queue_time histogram, burst_token_balance. Also per-org last_refill_ts.
Jordan: Agree. the console needs a timeline view: recent rejects by type, current token balance, and predicted throttle in next 5m (based on moving average).
Maria: UX for rollouts: start with soft enforcement (log-only + 429 shadow) for 2 weeks, then enable hard enforcement for low-risk orgs, then full rollout. enable per-org override for sales/SE.
Asha: Any concern about fairness during region failover? e.g., requests rerouted to another region doubling apparent concurrency.
Jordan: Router includes a regional affinity header; when failover occurs we short-circuit: we convert concurrency-cap checks to include a distributed lease (lightweight counter in our global cache) to avoid double-counting. fallback will temporarily reduce burst allowance.
Kevin: Config example (pseudo):
```
org_policy:
  rpm: 1200
  tpm: 30000
  concurrent_limit: 12
  burst_tokens: 4
  burst_window_sec: 60
  stream_pool_limit: 3
```
Jordan: Edge cases: queued requests timing out client-side — we should return Retry-After with queue position when queuing > 500ms. Also we should surface 'shadow 429s' in the console for debugging.
Maria: Ops: add an alert when global queue utilization > 60% and burst_token_drain_rate > 0.5 tokens/sec/org averaged across top 10 orgs.
Asha: Can we simulate with traffic replay before rollout? queueing behavior is subtle.
Jordan: Yes — I'll add a traffic-replay job that injects parallel streams + synthetic embeddings, sweeps concurrency and burst params. will produce a playbook for the rollout.
Kevin: OK. please add RFC + telemetry dashboard mockups. I can help wire up the alert rules.
Jordan: Will do. tagging @SRE-Bot to create an RFC issue and schedule a replay job. :white_check_mark: 
SRE-Bot: Created issue #INF-8342 "Hybrid per-org rate enforcement + burst token design" and scheduled replay job (replay-run-2026-03-20).
